question: to the Commission Bert-Jan Ruissen (ECR), Rihards Kols (ECR), Tomáš Kubín (PfE), Matej Tonin (PPE), Mieke Andriese (PfE), Fernand Kartheiser (NI), Alice Teodorescu Måwe (PPE), Tomáš Zdechovský (PPE), Geadis Geadi (ECR), Veronika Vrecionová (ECR), Ondřej Krutílek (ECR), Dick Erixon (ECR), Charlie Weimers (ECR), Beatrice Timgren (ECR), Elena Donazzan (ECR), Adrian-George Axinia (ECR), Jorge Martín Frías (PfE), Sebastian Tynkkynen (ECR), Antonio López-Istúriz White (PPE), Alexandr Vondra (ECR), François-Xavier Bellamy (PPE), Sander Smit (ECR) Subject:

On 16 March 2026, the Commission announced its provision of EUR 458 million in humanitarian assistance for the Middle East in 2026, including EUR 124 million committed to the West Bank and Gaza and EUR 100 million to Lebanon. Humanitarian assistance in these areas is delivered in highly complex environments. In Gaza, the de facto authorities are Hamas, while in large parts of southern Lebanon the armed group Hezbollah exercises significant influence. Given the risks of diversion in conflict environments, transparency regarding the channels and mechanisms through which EU funds are distributed is essential. 1.

Regarding the EUR 224 million allocated to the West Bank, Gaza and Lebanon, could the Commission specify the UN agencies and non-governmental organisations involved and the amount committed to each, including the local implementing partner organisations?
How much of these sums will be disbursed through cash-based assistance programmes, vouchers and/or direct transfers and could the Commission provide details on beneficiary lists and recommendations?

What monitoring, auditing and anti-diversion safeguards are in place, in addition to the EU restrictive measures list (which includes few Hamas and Hezbollah members), to ensure that EU funds do not directly or indirectly benefit Hamas, Hezbollah or affiliated entities?
answer: (English version) to the Commission Bert-Jan Ruissen (ECR), Rihards Kols (ECR), Tomáš Kubín (PfE), Matej Tonin (PPE), Mieke Andriese (PfE), Fernand Kartheiser (NI), Alice Teodorescu Måwe (PPE), Tomáš Zdechovský (PPE), Geadis Geadi (ECR), Veronika Vrecionová (ECR), Ondřej Krutílek (ECR), Dick Erixon (ECR), Charlie Weimers (ECR), Beatrice Timgren (ECR), Elena Donazzan (ECR), Adrian-George Axinia (ECR), Jorge Martín Frías (PfE), Sebastian Tynkkynen (ECR), Antonio López-Istúriz White (PPE), Alexandr Vondra (ECR), François-Xavier Bellamy (PPE), Sander Smit (ECR) (8 April 2026) Subject: Transparency of EU humanitarian funding to the West Bank, Gaza and Lebanon On 16 March 2026, the Commission announced its provision of EUR 458 million in humanitarian assistance for the Middle East in 2026, including EUR 124 million committed to the West Bank and Gaza and EUR 100 million to Lebanon. Humanitarian assistance in these areas is delivered in highly complex environments. In Gaza, the de facto authorities are Hamas, while in large parts of southern Lebanon the armed group Hezbollah exercises significant influence. Given the risks of diversion in conflict environments, transparency regarding the channels and mechanisms through which EU funds are distributed is essential. 1. Regarding the EUR 224 million allocated to the West Bank, Gaza and Lebanon, could the Commission specify the UN agencies and non-governmental organisations involved and the amount committed to each, including the local implementing partner organisations? 2. How much of these sums will be disbursed through cash-based assistance programmes, vouchers and/or direct transfers and could the Commission provide details on beneficiary lists and recommendations? 3. What monitoring, auditing and anti-diversion safeguards are in place, in addition to the EU restrictive measures list (which includes few Hamas and Hezbollah members), to ensure that EU funds do not directly or indirectly benefit Hamas, Hezbollah or affiliated entities? (5 June 2026) The Commission is contracting the funds announced on 16 March 2026, and therefore unable to give a list of selected humanitarian partners and the amount to be disbursed through cash-based assistance. The Commission is steadfast in its commitment to supporting humanitarian aid delivery that is principled and needs based. For this reason, it also supports the UN-led humanitarian coordination system to ensure all humanitarian efforts remain guided by international humanitarian law and humanitarian principles. The compliance with the Commission policy on cash assistance (1) is verified before selecting humanitarian partners to implement cash-based assistance programmes. The Commission is very much aware of the complex operational context in which EU-funded entities operate in the occupied Palestinian territory and Lebanon. This is why robust safeguards are in place, covering pre-funding due diligence and risk assessments (ex-ante checks), implementation monitoring, and post-funding oversight and controls (ex-post verification). Humanitarian partners are thoroughly assessed on their capacity to observe basic principles and obligations, including respect of the relevant EU, international and national laws, as well as compliance with transparency, accountability and internal controls. The Commission only works with pre-approved and certified humanitarian partners (2). Under Regulation (EU) 2024/2509 (3) laying down the financial rules applicable to the general budget of the Union, and in accordance with Article 138 thereof, the Commission applies strict safeguards to ensure that any person or entity involved in criminal activity, including terrorist financing and terrorist offences, is excluded from EU funding.
